    "Sharing one predicate (_kinds_mismatch) between the step-8a score and the card-swap guard, and failing open (None) when either side is unknown — single source of truth, no silent hard-filtering; do not change this shape.",

  "answers": {
    "q1": "The design is directionally sound — closed vocabulary, binary raw/processed regime, penalty-not-filter, fail-open on unknown — but the query-side regex is the weak link. Concrete failure modes: (1) both-regime mentions (including negations like 'I don't have raw spectra files') disable the penalty entirely, since both branches require the user to be in exactly one regime (F9); (2) 'other' kinds (vcf, peaks, fasta, gene_list…) can never mismatch, so e.g. VCF-vs-FASTQ is unprotected (F8); (3) ambiguous terms — 'beta values' (GWAS coefficients vs methylation), 'peak table' (ChIP-seq vs LC-MS) — misfire; (4) with ~4% label disagreement and a constant calibrated on one measured gap (17–24), about 1 in 25 fired penalties is wrong and, being effectively disqualifying, unrecoverable within scoring. A hard filter is strictly worse at that label error rate; a learned weight is premature given the evaluation n. Best improvement: derive the user's kinds from the actual attached file names/extensions first (the chat already stages attachments) and use prose regex only as fallback; second, when the penalty would flip the top card and the detection is prose-only, ask the user a one-line confirmation rather than silently re-ranking. Log every penalty firing so the constant 25 can be recalibrated on real traffic.",
    "q2": "Text should not override the backend's card. The reply is generated from the card, so when they diverge the text is as likely to be hallucinating as correcting — the original incident (reply inventing 'proteomicslfq for proteinGroups.txt') was exactly that. Right precedence: backend search + _llm_verify_routing owns the card; 6b is acceptable because it re-runs a selection among retrieved candidates with full context (a decision, not prose-following); 6d (the user explicitly named a pipeline) should win as user intent but still pass the input-compatibility check with a visible warning rather than silent refusal; 6c/6c-2 prose-following should be demoted to 'trigger a backend re-check of the mentioned candidate against the card' or removed. The new constraints (candidates-only + input-compatible) are the correct minimal fix and should stay — but when a swap is refused, the reply text must be repaired, otherwise the user still reads a recommendation for a workflow that cannot run on their data (F12).",
    "q3": "The sound parts: closed vocabulary with out-of-vocabulary rejection, verbatim constraint, guarded SQL, keep-on-failure, originals preserved, verifier instructed to use knowledge of the real tool, and walking the audit back to BioMate-authored rows after the DSS false confirmation. But 'two LLMs agree' is not adequate evidence on its own for a production catalog with no version control: the two models share training data and failure modes (the DSS example shows the verifier confirming a false positive from the upstream text itself). Add: (1) commit the proposals/verified JSONL, the updates.sql, and the DB md5 before/after to git — that is the only changelog this catalog has; (2) a small human spot-check with measured precision (e.g. 30 random agreed rows plus a sample of the 118 retag disagreements, which are currently discarded unread); (3) quantify the fine-grained input_kinds labels, not only the raw/processed class, if the +3 exact-kind boost is kept; (4) establish when the FTS corruption began, because per-row patches measured against a corrupt index may need re-review (F5). The guarded-SQL pattern itself is good and should be the template for all future catalog passes.",
